review_candidates.title: Stærkstrømsingeniør til langsigtede netanalyser og projektrelaterede analyser
review_candidates.location: Fredericia, Region of Southern Denmark, Denmark
review_candidates.description: Vil du være med til at planlægge eltransmissionsnettet, så Danmark kan integrere mere vedvarende energi og andre grønne teknologier – sikkert og effektivt? I Netplanlægning – El får du en central rolle i at identificere fremtidens behov og omsætte teknisk indsigt til konkrete løsninger, der kan mærkes i den grønne omstilling. Bliv en del af en afdeling med uformel tone og dygtige kolleger På kontoret i Fredericia er du en del af en fagligt velfunderet og uhøjtidelig afdeling med et højt specialiseret fagligt niveau og stor lyst til vidensdeling. Der er et fladt hierarki, og ledelsesstilen er præget af et højt fokus på motivation, trivsel og faglig udvikling. Vi prioriterer fleksibilitet – og du får tilbudt udstyr til en god hjemmearbejdsplads, så du kan veksle mellem at være på kontoret og arbejde hjemme under hensyntagen til opgavernes karakter og behovet for fysisk fremmøde. ”Færdighederne i afdelingen spænder bredt, hvilket giver god mulighed for at løse afdelingens opgaver og lære af hinanden. I afdelingen vægter vi samarbejdet og teamet højt, samtidig med at du kan udfolde dig inden for dit faglige interessefelt,” fortæller netplanlægningschef, Lars Højbjerg Nielsen. Analyser, der peger på behov og løsninger I Netplanlægning – El arbejder vi med at identificere behov og planlægge den overordnede netstruktur i eltransmissionsnettet. Det betyder, at vi har ansvar for analyser i forbindelse med nettilslutninger, vurderinger af kapacitetsforhold i transmissionsnettet, behovsidentifikation og langsigtet planlægning af netudbygninger. Dine primære opgaver er at: Udføre analyser, der identificerer langsigtede behov i eltransmissionsnettet og udarbejde løsningsforslag Udarbejde analyser og rationaler for konkrete nettilslutnings- og netudbygningsprojekter Understøtte projekter med analyser, dokumentation og beslutningsgrundlag Konkrete opgaver kan være: Samarbejde med netselskaber om netudbygning drevet af udviklingen i distributionsnettet Analysegrundlag og rationaler for nettilslutninger, reinvesteringer og netudbygninger Tekniske beskrivelser og input til samfundsøkonomiske analyser i forbindelse med investeringsbeslutninger Netberegninger i PowerFactory (fx load flow-simuleringer og kapacitetsberegninger) Dokumentation af langsigtede behov og omsætning til konkrete tiltag og udbygninger I rollen samarbejder du bredt – både internt med netplanlæggere, økonomer og projektledere samt eksternt med myn-digheder, netselskaber og kommecielle aktører. Sideløbende med analyseopgaverne bidrager du til at udvikle afdelingens metoder og værktøjer. “Vi står med en kæmpeopgave med at sikre tilstrækkelig kapacitet i eltransmissionsnettet. Din evne til at omsætte teknisk indsigt i netplanlægning til effektive løsninger og handling – og være med til at udvikle nye metoder til at kortlægge og kommunikere udbygningsbehovet – er afgørende for, at du kan levere gode resultater,” fortæller Lars. Speciale inden for simulering og analyse af elektriske systemer Du har en uddannelse som stærkstrømsingeniør med speciale inden for simulering og analyse af elektriske systemer – og vi hører meget gerne fra dig, uanset om du er nyuddannet eller har nogle års erfaring. Du har allerede erfaring med at anvende simuleringsværktøjet DIgSILENT PowerFactory. Ligeledes kan du arbejde struktureret med dataindsamling fra forskellige kilder og omsætte dette til konkrete resultater, fx ved at anvende programmering, scripts og Power BI. Branchekendskab og indsigt i samspillet mellem distributions- og transmissionsnettet i Danmark vægtes positivt. Det er en forudsætning, at du taler og skriver dansk og er god til at formidle informationer på en enkel og forståelig måde. Som person er du struktureret, analytisk dygtig og god til at prioritere. Du arbejder godt på egen hånd, men trives også i tæt og bredt samarbejde både internt og eksternt. Vil du være med til at gøre en forskel sammen med os? Så ser vi frem til at modtage din motiverede ansøgning og CV senest 29. november. Vi inviterer til samtale løbende, og tillader os at lukke rekrutteringen, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat. Vi holder 1. samtale online og 2. samtale i Fredericia. Er du nysgerrig på din kommende leder, eller har du spørgsmål til jobbet? Se nærmere på LinkedIn eller kontakt Lars Højbjerg Nielsen på tlf. +45 6124 4344. Særlige forhold: Da Energinet løser samfundskritiske opgaver, udfører vi baggrundstjek forud for ansættelsen. Det er en forudsætning for ansættelse, at dit baggrundstjek er foreneligt med ansættelse i Energinet. Baggrundstjekket gennemføres desuden én gang årligt. Vi ser mangfoldighed som en styrke og opfordrer alle kvalificerede, uanset baggrund, til at søge jobbet. Vi arbejder aktivt og målrettet med mangfoldighed i Energinet og opfordrer dig derfor til at udelade billede, oplysninger om alder, civilstand og lignende, for at minimere ubevidste biases i processen. Du kan læse mere om vores mangfoldighedspolitik her. Du bliver en del af Energinet Systemansvar, hvis kerneopgaver er at indpasse vedvarende energi, sikre lige adgang til nettene, udvikle markedsdesign, overvåge og balancere transmissionsnettet og at varetage forsyningssikkerheden i Danmark. Glæd dig til at blive en del af en organisation med et meningsfuldt formål, hvor vi forsyner Danmark med el og gas, og omstiller energisystemet til grøn energi. For at lykkes med den opgave, skal vi have dygtige og engagerede medarbejdere. Derfor har vi skabt rammer, hvor udvikling prioriteres, nye idéer bliver taget alvorligt, og der er balance mellem arbejde og privatliv. Vi kalder det Energi til mere, og du kan blive endnu klogere på det her

By choosing Qcells USA for turnkey solutions, customers can reduce uncertainty and risk, leading to enhanced investment returns and contributing to a more sustainable future. Qcells USA’s complete turnkey solutions seamlessly integrate the expertise of our Development, Module, and EPC teams, while ensuring close coordination with other vital internal groups such as Project Finance, Systems Integration, and Legal. As an integral part of the global Qcells brand, Qcells USA benefits from a legacy of excellence in photovoltaic manufacturing. This role is accountable for the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of integrated project controls systems encompassing cost control, schedule management, forecasting, change management, progress measurement, and project reporting -- ensuring that all active EPC projects are tracked and managed with accuracy, consistency, and transparency from Notice to Proceed through final close-out. maintain risk registers and support contingency management in coordination with Finance and project leadership Oversee the project close-out controls process including final cost reconciliation, lessons-learned capture, close-out reporting, and transition of project data to Finance for warranty reserve and asset accounting Drive the selection, implementation, and continuous improvement of project controls software, ERP integrations, and reporting automation tools to improve efficiency and data quality across the function Regular attendance, in accordance with company's attendance policy and supervisory assignment, is an essential job duty requirement for this position Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned by Management Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business, or a related field required; Ability to work independently, take ownership of technical solutions, prioritize tasks effectively, and proactively resolve issues. Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to participate in technical discussions and mentor other engineers. Experience building, deploying, and operating cloud-native or highly scalable backend services. Experience working within Agile/Scrum development environments. Hands-on experience using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or Codex) for code generation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and code review while applying sound engineering judgment to validate and improve generated output. Experience mentoring junior and mid-level engineers and contributing to engineering standards and best practices.

review_candidates.title: Senior Communications Officer - EMEEA
review_candidates.description: The Foundation We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally. The Team The Communications Division, led by the Chief Communications Officer in Seattle, oversees the foundation’s global communications strategy. The division brings together internal and external communications to advance the foundation’s mission of a more equitable world. The Global Communications team is responsible for shaping internal and external use of foundation voice to protect the foundation’s reputation and advance its priority advocacy and program objectives and ensure that employees are meaningfully connected to the foundation’s mission and community. The team is responsible for comprehensive voice planning for foundation leadership and key spokespeople as well as driving engagement with media. The Global Policy and Advocacy (GPA) Division’s mission is to understand the political context and policy debates affecting the foundation’s work, build support for our major program and policy objectives, and develop partnerships and alliances that can advance the foundation’s objectives nationally and globally. GPA works in close partnership with grantees, and with our colleagues in the Global Health, Global Development, Global Growth & Opportunity, Gender Equality divisions to build the environment in which all people have the opportunity to lead healthy and productive lives. Within the GPA division, the Europe, Middle East, and East Asia (EMEEA) team leads the foundation’s geographic presence in the largest donor countries outside North America and China, covering Europe (with a focus on UK, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Nordics, Netherlands, and European Union institutions), the Middle East (Arab League countries), and the Asia-Pacific region (Japan, South Korea, and Australia). EMEEA acts as the bridge between foundation teams and donor markets by offering deep insights on the geo-political landscape, media and public attitudes, and the foundation’s communication and advocacy priorities. EMEEA works alongside a network of grantees and partners - including, media, civil society organizations, think tanks, and academic institutions - to support the foundation’s overarching strategic goals. Your Role This Senior Communications Officer role is at the heart of delivering the Communication Division’s priorities, supporting the work of the GPA Division and driving the work of the EMEEA team. This is a fascinating, stretching, fast-paced, and diverse role with no one day the same. The successful application will develop and execute communication strategies for the foundation’s work in France, Italy, Spain, and Arab League countries in the Middle East - to support the brand, reputation and advocacy goals of the foundation. This involves gaining a deep understanding of those countries listed - how they work, their priorities, audiences, and communications landscape. The strategies developed and implemented will cover everything from leadership visits and voice planning, to writing key messages, editorial planning, and creative content creation. They will be informed by audience insights and have measurement and evaluation embedded from the outset. The role would suit someone who is experienced, full of innovative ideas, energy, and enthusiasm who has a track record of working well with others to get things done. Increasingly the role requires a campaigning mindset and approach to ensure cut-through and impact. Full professional proficiency in French and English is an essential requirement for this role. Arabic is highly desirable. Based in the foundation’s London office, the postholder will be expected to undertake regular international travel, including to the countries referenced above and, occasionally, to the foundation’s headquarters in Seattle. The role will report to the Deputy Director, EMEEA Communications, who is also based in London. The postholder will work closely with other Senior Communications Officers across EMEEA, the Insights and Measurement and Digital Content and Partnerships leads, and colleagues across the wider Global Communications team. The role will also involve extensive collaboration with Seattle-based stakeholders, external partners and grantees to ensure alignment, strengthen coordination and advance the foundation’s communications priorities across the region. What You’ll Do You will draw on your knowledge and skills to provide communications counsel to programmatic colleagues, grantees, and partners, and work together to build awareness and support for the foundation's work and programmatic, policy, advocacy, and communications goals. You will develop and manage a portfolio of grants and contracts to achieve this and build and maintain a network of relationships, including with senior leaders. There is a lot of space for creative and innovative thinking, working collaboratively with new and existing partners to find ways to get attention and capture the attention of audiences. To achieve this, you must balance strategic thinking, whilst remaining nimble and opportunistic. Drawing on your knowledge of the communications landscape in each country and the most impactful distribution approaches, together with colleagues across the foundation you will agree communication goals and draft strategies that will enable and support the foundation’s objectives - leveraging print and digital channels - to build and sustain the right kind of momentum for the programs. Proactively manage all media relations, PR, enquiries, relationships at senior levels, cultivate partnerships with creators, influencers and the entertainment sector, and a full spectrum of media. This requires good judgement, risk management, and the ability to flex. Work with partners and foundation colleagues to develop narratives, key messages, research data, and ensure this is used to develop content at key moments. Work with the government and grantees in country communication to elevate priority issues and manage issues that may be reputational risks for the foundation. Ensure strategic communications campaigns are coherent, well-designed, and creative, so they have impact and build momentum. Develop a coalition of third-party voices and messengers to elevate priority issues and build strategies to align voices and narrative. Ensure core communications material and collateral are market ready and used. You will manage vendors and grantees to ensure collaborative and successful delivery of objectives, always with an eye to robust resource management and RoI. Develop messaging and support leadership trips, including speaking and media opportunities. By Doing This You Will Help Achieve Stronger awareness among target audiences of key foundation policy positions. An enabling environment to encourage increased political and public commitment to international development, global health and/or accountability for past commitments. Strengthened communications partnership with government and other institutions. Strengthened profile of foundation local leadership among target audiences and knowledge and trust in the foundation and its work. Your Experience A bachelor’s degree and senior-level experience in journalism, communications, public relations, public policy or a related field. Excellent experience of working with a full range of media, including print, broadcast and digital in the countries listed above. Plus, event management and execution experience. A proven track record of leading complex communications initiatives, providing strategic counsel to senior stakeholders, and managing executive communications and reputational risks, ideally within complex, matrixed organizations. Experience working with government institutions and/or public/NGO institutions is desirable. Experience in devising and leading communication campaigns that are creative and have impact. A demonstrable understanding of global and local politics - particularly in France and/or the Middle East, a strong analytical mindset to understand and react to real-time data and insights, and excellent judgement. Full professional proficiency in French and English. Arabic is highly desirable. Strong communication skills, both written and oral, and the ability to influence and engage individuals at all levels internally and externally. Ability to assimilate and understand complex new subjects, including scientific, medical and development of finance policy areas. Ability to confidently represent the foundation when dealing with media, and exercising sound media judgment. Confidence in working in a fast-paced environment under tight deadlines, with a demonstrated ability to juggle multiple and competing demands and establish priorities, remain flexible, and work collaboratively as part of a team. Ability to effectively cultivate and manage relationships both with internal staff and foundation partners. Other Attributes Comfortable in a wide range of cultural, geographic and operational situations, demonstrating culturally sensitive behaviour with a diverse range of people and a deep commitment to development issues and high standards of personal integrity. Ability to travel 30-40% to France, Southern Europe, Middle East and the US. Application deadline: 21 November 2026 Hiring Requirements As part of our standard hiring process for new employees, employment will be contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Candidate Accommodations We’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for all candidates. If you have a disability or medical condition and need an accommodation at any stage of the application or interview process—such as an ASL interpreter, alternative interview format, or physical accessibility support—we’re happy to help. Please contact HR@gatesfoundation.org with the position number and a brief description of your accommodation needs. Requests will be handled confidentially. Inclusion Statement We are dedicated to the belief that all lives have equal value. We strive for a global and cultural workplace that supports ever greater diversity, equity, and inclusion — of voices, ideas, and approaches — and we support this diversity through all our employment practices. All applicants and employees who are drawn to serve our mission will enjoy equality of opportunity and fair treatment without regard to race, color, age, religion, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, disability, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and prior protected activity.

Support inspection and audit readiness activities. Drive communication and coordination across study teams located in North America, Europe and APAC regions. Contribute to the ongoing development and scaling of the clinical operations function. Ability to work independently with minimal infrastructure and high levels of accountability. Flexibility to support meetings and collaborations across US time zones when required. Highly Desirable Experience in ultra-rare diseases. Dermatology clinical trial experience. Experience managing global studies with small patient populations. Remote-based position in the UK or Republic of Ireland. Opportunity to make a significant impact within a growing, well-funded biotech. Exposure to pivotal-stage development programmes with potential registration milestones. Location Remote within the United Kingdom or Republic of Ireland . Candidates must be willing to support occasional meetings outside standard business hours to accommodate global study teams and CRO partners based in the United States.
